stories.title: Read NIfTI files (.nii and .nii.gz) in the converter
stories.description: Create tools/anatomy/nifti.ts: a small reader for NIfTI-1 files, plain or gzipped (Node's built-in zlib). It returns the volume's size, voxel spacing, the position/direction information from the file header (the sform or qform 'affine'), and the voxel values as numbers with the header's scale and offset applied (scl_slope, scl_inter). Support the data types CT scans and masks use — unsigned 8-bit, signed and unsigned 16-bit, 32-bit float — in both byte orders, and reject anything else (wrong header size or magic text, more than 3 dimensions with size > 1, unsupported type, file shorter than the header says) with a clear error naming the file. Add a test helper in tests/anatomy/ (not in src/ or tools/) that writes a tiny NIfTI file from an array, so tests can build fixtures. Plain TypeScript run in Node (no browser code); only Node's built-in modules, no new dependencies. Tests build their tiny input files in memory or in a temporary folder (never real CT data, nothing downloaded).
acceptance: Unit test: a generated 4×3×2 signed 16-bit .nii file is read back with the right size, spacing and every voxel value
Unit test: the same file gzipped (.nii.gz) reads back identically
Unit test: scale and offset in the header are applied (stored 100 with slope 2 and intercept −1024 reads as −824)
Unit test: 8-bit and 32-bit float files and a big-endian file read back correctly
Unit test: a file with a wrong magic text, an unsupported data type, or fewer bytes than the header promises is rejected with an error that names the file
stories.notes: Done. tools/anatomy/nifti.ts exports readNifti(path) and parseNifti(bytes, name). Data comes back as Float32Array in file order (i fastest); affine is 4x4 rows in NIfTI RAS+ (sform > qform > spacing-only), affineSource says which. Fixture helper: tests/anatomy/niftiFixture.ts (makeNifti / writeNifti).

stories.title: Map CT numbers (Hounsfield units) to 8-bit intensity over a documented window
stories.description: Create tools/anatomy/intensity.ts with the function that turns a CT number (HU) into the 8-bit intensity stored in region files: a straight-line mapping over a window, default −1000 HU → 0 and +2000 HU → 255, rounded, clamped outside the window. The window is a named, documented setting that the converter can be given other values for (lower must be below upper, both finite — otherwise a clear error). Plain TypeScript run in Node (no browser code); only Node's built-in modules, no new dependencies.
acceptance: Unit test: with the default window −1000 → 0, +2000 → 255, and +500 → 128 (within 1)
Unit test: values below the window give 0 and values above give 255
Unit test: over −1500 … +2500 HU in steps of 1 the result never decreases as HU rises
Unit test: a custom window (e.g. −200 … +1500) maps its ends to 0 and 255
Unit test: a window whose lower end is not below its upper end, or NaN, is rejected with a clear error
stories.notes: Done. tools/anatomy/intensity.ts: DEFAULT_HU_WINDOW {lower:-1000, upper:2000}, makeHuWindow(lower, upper) (validates), huToIntensity(hu, window?), huVolumeToIntensity(array, window?) -> Uint8Array. NaN HU maps to 0.

stories.title: Reorder voxels into the app's one standard layout
stories.description: Create tools/anatomy/standardLayout.ts. Every region file is written in the standard layout the phantom uses (owner decision 2026-11-10), so no other zone has to deal with file layouts: voxel axis i runs toward the patient's left (+x), j toward the back (+y), k toward the head (+z), i.e. the Volume's orientation is the identity. NIfTI positions are in 'RAS' coordinates (x = patient's right, y = front, z = head), so app x = −NIfTI x, app y = −NIfTI y, app z = NIfTI z. Using the affine from the header, work out which stored axis points along which patient direction, then swap and flip the axes of the voxel array (and the spacing) to the standard layout, and compute the Volume origin (patient position of the centre of voxel (0, 0, 0)). CT and mask volumes go through the same function. If an axis is tilted more than 5° away from every patient axis (an oblique scan), stop with a clear error rather than guess. Plain TypeScript run in Node (no browser code); only Node's built-in modules, no new dependencies. Tests build their tiny input files in memory or in a temporary folder (never real CT data, nothing downloaded).
acceptance: Unit test: one small asymmetric test volume stored in four different axis orders/directions (including the common 'RAS' and 'LPS' ones) gives exactly the same voxel array, spacing and origin after reordering
Unit test: a voxel known to be at the patient's left-back-head corner ends up at the highest i, j and k
Unit test: different spacing on each axis follows its axis through the reordering
Unit test: an affine tilted by 20° is rejected with a clear error; one tilted by 1° is accepted
stories.notes: Done. tools/anatomy/standardLayout.ts: planStandardLayout(size, rasAffine) -> LayoutPlan (outSize, spacing, origin in app frame), applyLayoutPlan(plan, data) keeps the array type, toStandardLayout({size, affine, data}) does both. Rejects axes tilted > MAX_AXIS_TILT_DEG (5°) and two axes along one patient direction.

stories.title: Map the dataset's masks to our tissue labels through a mapping table
stories.description: Create tools/anatomy/label-map.json and tools/anatomy/labels.ts. The input is a CT plus one yes/no mask file per structure, named as in the TotalSegmentator dataset (e.g. vertebrae_L4, sacrum, hip_left, spinal_cord, aorta, inferior_vena_cava, iliac_artery_left, autochthon_left). The table maps each mask name to one of our tissue labels (src/core/labels.ts, read-only) and, for bones, to a vertebral level (used by the next story). Draft mapping: vertebrae, sacrum and hip bones → bone; spinal_cord → thecal sac; aorta and iliac arteries → artery; vena cava and iliac veins → vein; muscles → muscle. In this story every bone voxel is labelled cancellous bone and voxels covered by no mask stay air; F1-S25 then splits cortical from cancellous bone and labels the unmasked voxels from their CT number. Mask names not in the table are ignored and listed in the converter's report; where masks overlap, bone wins, then the table's order. The table carries "reviewedByOwner": false (only the owner changes it) and a note that the mask names must be re-checked against the real download in F1.7 (loops have no network access). Plain TypeScript run in Node (no browser code); only Node's built-in modules, no new dependencies. Tests build their tiny input files in memory or in a temporary folder (never real CT data, nothing downloaded).
acceptance: Unit test: label-map.json is valid: every target label is a key of TISSUE, every bone entry has a level from LEVEL_CODES, and reviewedByOwner is false
Unit test: on a generated fixture (a CT plus masks for two vertebrae, the canal, an artery and a vein) each masked voxel gets the mapped label
Unit test: where a bone mask and another mask overlap the voxel is bone; where two non-bone masks overlap the first in the table's order wins
Unit test: a mask whose name is not in the table changes nothing and is reported; a mask whose size differs from the CT's is rejected with a clear error
stories.notes: Done. tools/anatomy/label-map.json (status draft, reviewedByOwner false, entries [{mask, tissue, level?}]) and tools/anatomy/labels.ts: loadLabelMap(), validateLabelMap(obj) -> problems[], labelsFromMasks(ctSize, masks[{name,size,data}], map) -> {labels, ignored}. Ribs and other TotalSegmentator masks not in the table are ignored and reported (ribs have no LEVEL_CODES entry) - owner may want to review in F1.7.

stories.title: Split cortical from cancellous bone and label unmasked voxels from their CT number
stories.description: Extend tools/anatomy/labels.ts and tools/anatomy/label-map.json (split out of F1-S4 at the 2026-11-10 story review). Bone voxels become cortical bone at or above a CT-number threshold in the table and cancellous bone below it. Voxels covered by no mask get a fallback label from their CT number, with thresholds in the table: air, skin/fat or muscle (generic soft tissue). Voxels labelled by a non-bone mask are left alone. The thresholds are draft numbers for the owner to review (the table keeps "reviewedByOwner": false). Plain TypeScript run in Node (no browser code); only Node's built-in modules, no new dependencies. Tests build their tiny input files in memory or in a temporary folder (never real CT data, nothing downloaded).
acceptance: Unit test: bone voxels at or above the threshold are cortical, below it cancellous
Unit test: unmasked voxels become air, skin/fat or muscle according to their CT number
Unit test: a voxel labelled by a non-bone mask (canal, artery, vein, muscle) keeps its label whatever its CT number
Unit test: the thresholds in label-map.json are finite numbers in rising order (air < skin/fat < muscle; one bone threshold), and reviewedByOwner is still false
Unit test: the earlier tests in tests/anatomy/labels.test.ts still pass unchanged
stories.notes: Done. label-map.json gained "thresholds" {bone.corticalFromHu 600, unmasked airFromHu -1000 / skinFatFromHu -250 / muscleFromHu -20} (draft, for owner review) and "thresholdsNote". labels.ts: validateThresholds(map), refineLabelsByHu(labels, hu, thresholds) -> new Uint8Array; loadLabelMap checks both. Unmasked dense voxels (e.g. ribs, not in the table) become muscle, as the story asks.

stories.title: Build the vertebral-level volume for bone voxels
stories.description: In tools/anatomy/labels.ts also build the level volume: for every voxel, the level id (LEVEL_IDS in src/core/labels.ts) of the bone it belongs to — C1…C7, T1…T12, L1…L5, sacrum, ilium (both hip bones) — taken from the mapping table, and 0 (NO_LEVEL) for every voxel that is not bone.
acceptance: Unit test on the fixture: every bone voxel (cortical or cancellous) has a level other than 0
Unit test on the fixture: no non-bone voxel has a level
Unit test: the voxels of the vertebrae_L4 mask get the id of L4, sacrum → 'sacrum', hip_left and hip_right → 'ilium'
Unit test: where two bone masks overlap, each voxel still gets exactly one level (the first in the table's order)
stories.notes: Done. labels.ts: levelsFromMasks(labels, masks, map) -> Uint8Array of LEVEL_IDS; first bone mask in table order wins on overlap; non-bone voxels forced to NO_LEVEL. Call it with the refined labels (after refineLabelsByHu).

stories.title: Cut the volume down to one region
stories.description: Create tools/anatomy/regions.ts with the three regions and their level ranges — cervical C1–T1, thoracic T1–L1, lumbosacral L1–sacrum including both SI joints — and a function that crops the intensity, label and level volumes to a box around a region: the bounding box of the bone voxels of the region's levels (for lumbosacral also the ilium voxels within a documented distance of the sacrum, so both SI joints are inside, and the upper part of both hip bones up to the top of the iliac crests — owner decision 2026-11-10: the crests are landmarks and they overlap L5–S1 on oblique views; the lower part of the hip bones may be cut off), plus a documented margin on every side that is limited by the volume's edges, and that always reaches the skin at the back when the scan includes it (needles enter there). The origin is updated so every voxel keeps its patient position. If none of the region's levels is in the scan, stop with a clear error; report which of the region's levels are missing. Plain TypeScript run in Node (no browser code); only Node's built-in modules, no new dependencies. Tests build their tiny input files in memory or in a temporary folder (never real CT data, nothing downloaded).
acceptance: Unit test: the three regions have exactly the level ranges above
Unit test: on a fixture with five stacked 'vertebrae', cropping to a region covering three of them keeps all their bone voxels and the margin, and drops the far parts of the other two
Unit test: a voxel has the same patient position (origin + index × spacing) before and after cropping
Unit test: for lumbosacral, ilium voxels next to the sacrum are inside the crop, and so is the highest ilium voxel on each side (the iliac crests)

Unit test: on a fixture with a skin/fat layer behind the bones, the outermost skin voxel behind the region's bones is inside the crop; when the scan ends before the skin, the crop ends at the scan's edge without an error
Unit test: a region with none of its levels present is rejected with a clear error; missing levels are reported
stories.notes: Done. tools/anatomy/regions.ts: REGIONS (name, title, levels, includesIlium), CROP_MARGIN_MM = 10, SI_JOINT_DISTANCE_MM = 30 (box-shaped, per axis), cropToRegion(vol, region, {marginMm?, siJointDistanceMm?}) -> cropped {size, spacing, origin, intensity, labels, levels, box, missingLevels}. Lumbosacral keeps ilium within 30 mm of the sacrum and all ilium from the sacrum bottom upward (crests). Back reach = furthest-back non-air voxel in the box columns + margin. For the owner (F1.7): on a real supine CT the scanner table may count as non-air and stretch the crop backwards; check when converting real data.

stories.title: Resample a volume to a target voxel size
stories.description: Create tools/anatomy/resample.ts: resample a volume in the standard layout to a target voxel spacing (a converter setting, default 1.0 mm on every axis), so region files stay within the 25 MB limit and tablet memory. Intensity uses straight-line (trilinear) interpolation; label and level volumes use the nearest voxel, so no made-up in-between labels appear. The patient position of the anatomy must not shift. Plain TypeScript run in Node (no browser code); only Node's built-in modules, no new dependencies. Tests build their tiny input files in memory or in a temporary folder (never real CT data, nothing downloaded).
acceptance: Unit test: resampling a 2 mm volume to 1 mm doubles the voxel count along each axis (±1) and the header reports 1 mm spacing
Unit test: a volume already at the target spacing comes back unchanged
Unit test: the centre of a small bright block is at the same patient position (within half a voxel) before and after
Unit test: the resampled label and level volumes contain only values that were in the originals
Unit test: a target spacing that is zero, negative or not a number is rejected with a clear error
stories.notes: Done. tools/anatomy/resample.ts: DEFAULT_TARGET_SPACING_MM = 1, checkTargetSpacing(number | {x,y,z}), resampleVolume({size, spacing, origin, intensity, labels, levels?}, target) -> same shape. Origin (first voxel centre) unchanged; output count per axis = floor((n-1)*s/t)+1; same spacing returns copies.

stories.title: Define and write the region file format (JSON header plus gzipped 8-bit data)
stories.description: Create src/anatomy/regionFormat.ts (shared by the converter and the browser loader; plain TypeScript with no Node-only or browser-only code) and tools/anatomy/writeRegion.ts. A region is a set of files named after the region: <region>.json (header: format version, region name, size, voxel spacing, origin, orientation — always the identity — and the names and uncompressed byte lengths of the data files), <region>.intensity.bin.gz, <region>.labels.bin.gz and <region>.levels.bin.gz (each 8 bits per voxel, in the Volume's index order i + size.x × (j + size.y × k), gzipped). regionFormat.ts holds the header type and a validator that checks every field by hand (no schema library) and returns clear error messages. writeRegion.ts writes the set into a folder with Node's built-in zlib. Region names are limited to lower-case letters, digits and dashes (they become file names). Tests build their tiny input files in memory or in a temporary folder (never real CT data, nothing downloaded).
acceptance: Unit test: writing a small volume and reading the files back (gunzip + header) gives the same size, spacing, origin and every intensity, label and level value

Unit test: the header validator accepts the written header and rejects a missing field, a non-positive spacing, a size that does not match the data length, a non-identity orientation, and a region name with other characters
Unit test: each data file's uncompressed length equals size.x × size.y × size.z
stories.notes: Done. src/anatomy/regionFormat.ts: REGION_FORMAT_VERSION 1, RegionHeader {formatVersion, region, size, spacing, origin, orientation (identity, as Vec3 list), files {intensity|labels|levels: {name, bytes}}}, validateRegionHeader -> string[], parseRegionHeader (throws), isValidRegionName, headerFileName, dataFileName. tools/anatomy/writeRegion.ts: writeRegion(folder, {region, size, spacing, origin, intensity, labels, levels}) -> {header, paths}.

stories.title: Make the converter command turn a NIfTI folder into a region file set
stories.description: Replace the placeholder in tools/anatomy/convert.ts with the real converter (the command npm run anatomy:convert already exists; package.json must not change). The input folder holds ct.nii.gz (or ct.nii), a segmentations/ folder with one mask file per structure, and a small source.json written by hand: { region, sourceDataset, licence, attribution, optional window and voxel spacing }. Steps: read → standard layout → intensity window → labels and levels → crop to the region → resample → write the region file set into the output folder; then print a short report (region, size, spacing, file sizes, ignored masks, missing levels). The usage line and error exit for missing arguments must keep working (tests/anatomy/convert-cli.test.ts stays untouched). Validate everything that comes from outside: both folders and the files must exist, source.json fields are checked, the region must be one of the three known ones; never build a shell command from input. Problems end with a clear message and an error exit code, without half-written output. Plain TypeScript run in Node (no browser code); only Node's built-in modules, no new dependencies. Tests build their tiny input files in memory or in a temporary folder (never real CT data, nothing downloaded).
acceptance: Unit test: running the converter on a generated fixture folder (a tiny CT and masks in a temporary folder) writes a region file set whose header equals the expected header and whose intensity, label and level voxels equal the expected values
Unit test: run with no arguments it still prints the usage line containing '<input-folder> <output-folder>' and exits with an error code (the existing test passes unchanged)
Unit test: a missing input folder, a missing ct file, a broken source.json and an unknown region each give a clear message and an error exit code, and write no region files
Unit test: the report names masks that were ignored because they are not in the mapping table
stories.notes: Done. Logic in tools/anatomy/convertCore.ts (USAGE, readSourceInfo, convertFolder(in, out) -> ConvertReport {source, header, files, ignoredMasks, missingLevels}, formatReport, runConvertCli(args, out) -> exit code); tools/anatomy/convert.ts only calls runConvertCli. Output folder must already exist; files are written to a .partial-* scratch folder inside it and moved into place only when everything succeeded. Masks must match the CT size and affine. For F1.7: readNifti keeps a Float32 copy of each mask, so a full-size real CT with ~100 masks is read one mask at a time (each turned into 0/1 bytes straight away) — watch memory on very large scans.

stories.title: Find each vertebra's body centre and endplates
stories.description: Create tools/anatomy/landmarks.ts. From the label and level volumes, compute for each typical vertebral level present (C3 … L5; see the note on other levels) the body centre and the superior and inferior endplates (centre and tilt direction as a unit vector pointing away from the body), in the shared LevelLandmarks format (src/core/types.ts, read-only). Suggested approach: the body is the part of the level's bone in front of the spinal canal (the canal is where the thecal sac / spinal cord voxels are); the endplates are its top and bottom faces. Results are approximations for the owner to review on real anatomy; tests check them on the phantom, whose true landmarks are known (createPhantomLandmarks). C1 and C2 (no normal body) are left out for now (open question for the owner). The sacrum and the hip bones are not LevelLandmarks entries either: they get their own landmarks in F1-S23 (owner decision 2026-11-10). Plain TypeScript run in Node (no browser code); only Node's built-in modules, no new dependencies.
acceptance: Unit test on the phantom: for L4 and L5 the computed body centre is within 3 mm of createPhantomLandmarks()
Unit test on the phantom: each endplate centre is within 3 mm, and each endplate direction within 10°, of the phantom's
Unit test: at every computed body centre the label is bone and the level volume has that level
Unit test: a volume with no levels gives an empty list, and C1, C2, sacrum and ilium are skipped without an error
stories.notes: Done. tools/anatomy/landmarks.ts: TYPICAL_LEVELS (C3…L5), boneVoxelsByLevel, bodyVoxels (level bone with y in front of the canal = thecalSac/spinalCord voxels in the level's slices; without canal, the front 40% of the bone depth), centreInside (mean, snapped to the nearest body voxel if outside), findBodyLandmarks(vol) -> [{level, bodyCentre, superiorEndplate, inferiorEndplate}] head to foot. Endplates: least-squares plane through the top/bottom voxel of each body column at least 75% as tall as the tallest. For owner review on real data: if the real spinal_cord mask stops above the lumbar levels, the 40%-front fallback is used there.

stories.title: Find each vertebra's pedicle centres and the foramen centres, including L5–S1
stories.description: Extend tools/anatomy/landmarks.ts with, for each level from F1-S10, the left and right pedicle centres (the bone bridges joining the body to the back part of the vertebra, on either side of the canal) and the foramen centres on both sides. A foramen is the opening between this level's pedicle and the pedicle of the level below, beside the canal; it is listed under the level ABOVE it (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md → Landmark levels), so the lowest level in a volume has none — except L5 when the sacrum is in the volume (owner decision 2026-11-10): the L5–S1 foramen is the opening between L5's pedicle and the top of the sacrum beside the canal, and it is listed under L5. Without it the real lumbosacral region would have no L5 nerve root. The phantom has no sacrum, so add a small generated 'pelvis fixture' helper in tests/anatomy/ (an 'L5' block shaped like the phantom's lower block, a 'sacrum' block below it, and an 'ilium' block on each side of the sacrum with a narrow gap and a highest point; its true landmark positions are exported). F1-S23 and F1-S15 reuse it. 'left' is the patient's left (+x). Plain TypeScript run in Node (no browser code); only Node's built-in modules, no new dependencies.
acceptance: Unit test on the phantom: the pedicle centres of L4 and L5, left and right, are within 3 mm of createPhantomLandmarks()

Unit test on the phantom: L4 has a left and a right foramen centre within 4 mm of the phantom's (the phantom's own foramen point is not exactly midway between the pedicles, so 4 mm rather than 3); L5 (the lowest level, no sacrum in the phantom) has none
Unit test: left landmarks have a larger x than right ones
Unit test: no foramen centre lies in a bone voxel

Unit test on the pelvis fixture: L5 has a left and a right foramen centre; each lies below (−z) L5's pedicle centre and above the top of the sacrum on its side, within 4 mm of the fixture's known point, and in a non-bone voxel
stories.notes: Done. landmarks.ts: findLevelParts(vol) -> body + endplates + pedicleCentre + optional foramenCentre per typical level. Pedicle = level bone in the canal's front-to-back range, beside the canal, up to PEDICLE_REACH_MM (10) past its side wall (stand-in canal behind the body if no canal voxels). Foramen = under the pedicle's (x, y), midway between the pedicle bottom and the highest bone of the next level (L5 -> sacrum) in the pedicle's footprint columns, moved off bone if needed. Pelvis fixture: tests/anatomy/pelvisFixture.ts (createPelvisFixture({topZ?}), PELVIS_TRUTH incl. sacrum, crests, SI gap, L5-S1 facet gap).

stories.title: Find each vertebra's superior articular process tips
stories.description: Extend tools/anatomy/landmarks.ts with the left and right superior articular process tips of each level from F1-S10: the highest points of the bony pillars behind and beside the canal that reach up to the facet joint with the level above. This completes the LevelLandmarks entry; add the function that returns the whole Landmarks object for a region. Plain TypeScript run in Node (no browser code); only Node's built-in modules, no new dependencies.
acceptance: Unit test on the phantom: the superior articular process tips of L4 and L5, left and right, are within 3 mm of createPhantomLandmarks()
Unit test: every tip lies in or within 1.5 mm of a bone voxel of its own level
Unit test on the phantom: the complete Landmarks object has the region name, the levels L4 and L5 in head-to-foot order, and every required field of LevelLandmarks
stories.notes: Done. landmarks.ts: superior articular tips = highest level-bone voxels behind the canal (j > canal back) and beside it (past its side wall, up to ARTICULAR_REACH_MM 20), middle of those top voxels snapped onto one; findLevelLandmarks(vol) -> complete LevelLandmarks[]; computeLandmarks(vol) -> Landmarks {region, levels}. A level whose tips cannot be found on both sides is left out.

stories.title: Find the sacrum's landmarks and the top of each iliac crest
stories.description: Extend tools/anatomy/landmarks.ts (owner decision 2026-11-10: add the sacrum and the iliac crests). When the volume has sacrum bone, fill Landmarks.sacrum in the shared SacrumLandmarks format (src/core/types.ts, read-only): the superior endplate of S1 (the top face of the part of the sacrum in front of the canal: its centre, and its tilt direction as a unit vector pointing up, away from the sacrum) and the left and right tips of S1's superior articular processes (the highest points of the sacrum's pillars behind and beside the canal). When the volume has hip-bone ('ilium') voxels on both sides, fill Landmarks.iliacCrest with the highest (+z) point of the hip bone on each side; 'left' is the patient's left (+x), judged from the midline of the sacrum or canal. If a hip bone reaches the top edge of the volume its crest is cut off: leave iliacCrest out altogether and say so in the returned report rather than guess. A volume without sacrum or hip bones simply gets neither field. The sacral hiatus and SI-joint points are NOT part of this story (they come with the caudal and SI-joint procedures, F10). Results are approximations for the owner to review on real anatomy; tests use the pelvis fixture from F1-S11. Plain TypeScript run in Node (no browser code); only Node's built-in modules, no new dependencies.
acceptance: Unit test on the pelvis fixture: the sacrum's superior endplate centre is within 3 mm, and its direction within 10°, of the fixture's known values; the direction is a unit vector with z > 0
Unit test on the pelvis fixture: the left and right S1 superior articular process tips are within 3 mm of the fixture's, and each lies in or within 1.5 mm of a sacrum bone voxel
Unit test on the pelvis fixture: the left and right iliac crest points are within 3 mm of the fixture's highest hip-bone points, and the left one has the larger x
Unit test on the phantom (no sacrum, no hip bones): the Landmarks object has neither a sacrum nor an iliacCrest field, and nothing fails
Unit test: when a hip bone touches the top edge of the volume, iliacCrest is left out and the report says the crest is cut off
Unit test: the earlier landmark tests still pass unchanged
stories.notes: Done. landmarks.ts: computeRegionLandmarks(vol) -> {landmarks, notes}; computeLandmarks now returns its .landmarks. Sacrum: top S1_DEPTH_MM (35) of sacrum bone; endplate = plane fit on body columns within 2 canal half-widths of the midline (keeps the wings out); SAP tips as for vertebrae. Iliac crest: highest ilium voxels each side of the sacral canal midline (else any canal, else the volume centre); left out with a note if a side is missing or touches the top edge.

stories.title: Model the epidural space and the ligamentum flavum
stories.description: Create tools/anatomy/softTissue.ts, the soft-tissue modeller: CT segmentations do not contain these structures, so they are added as approximate shapes. This story: inside the bony canal, label the voxels between the thecal sac and the canal wall as epidural space; at each gap between two neighbouring laminae (the back wall of the canal between two levels) add a ligamentum flavum layer of a set thickness behind the epidural space. Between two vertebrae the canal has no bony ring, so carry the canal's outline across the gap. (Modelling a missing thecal sac is the next story, F1-S26.) The numbers that shape it live in tools/anatomy/soft-tissue-params.json with "reviewedByOwner": false; only the owner changes that flag. The modeller changes tissue labels only, never the intensity (these structures are invisible on X-ray) and never a bone voxel. Tests run on the phantom with its modelled soft tissue removed (helper in tests/anatomy/: ligamentum flavum, epidural space, nerve root, artery, vein and joint-space voxels turned back into muscle; bone, disc, thecal sac and spinal cord kept). Plain TypeScript run in Node (no browser code); only Node's built-in modules, no new dependencies.
acceptance: Unit test on the stripped phantom: after modelling, the straight midline line from the back to the front (PHANTOM_TEST_POINTS.midlineLine) crosses skin → muscle → ligamentum flavum → epidural space → thecal sac, in that order (the F0.4 check)
Unit test: no bone voxel changed its label and the intensity volume is unchanged
Unit test: soft-tissue-params.json has reviewedByOwner false
Unit test: running the modeller twice gives the same result as running it once
stories.notes: Done. tools/anatomy/soft-tissue-params.json (draft, reviewedByOwner false: canal.maxAreaMm2 1500, ligamentumFlavum.thicknessMm 4). tools/anatomy/softTissue.ts: loadSoftTissueParams(), modelSoftTissue(vol, landmarks?, params?) -> copy with new labels (steps so far: canal), modelCanal(vol, labels, params). Canal per slice = 4-connected non-bone region grown from thecal sac/cord; open (edge or too big) slices use the nearest closed slice outline (union if equally near); ligamentum flavum only in open slices between two closed ones, behind the outline, stopping at bone. Only air/skinFat/muscle (and earlier epidural/LF) are overwritten.

stories.title: Model the thecal sac when the scan has none
stories.description: Extend the soft-tissue modeller (split out of F1-S13 at the 2026-11-10 story review): if the volume has no thecal sac voxels at all, model one as a tube down the middle of the bony canal, as the first modelling step (before the epidural space and ligamentum flavum of F1-S13). A volume that already has a thecal sac is left exactly as it is by this step. The numbers that shape it live in tools/anatomy/soft-tissue-params.json with "reviewedByOwner": false; only the owner changes that flag. The modeller changes tissue labels only, never the intensity (these structures are invisible on X-ray) and never a bone voxel. Tests run on the stripped phantom from F1-S13 with the thecal sac and spinal cord also turned into muscle. Plain TypeScript run in Node (no browser code); only Node's built-in modules, no new dependencies.
acceptance: Unit test: with the thecal sac and cord removed, a thecal sac is modelled inside the canal: it has voxels at every vertebral level's height, none in bone and none outside the canal
Unit test: after the full modelling run on that volume, the midline order from F1-S13 holds (skin → muscle → ligamentum flavum → epidural space → thecal sac)
Unit test: a volume that already has thecal sac voxels is unchanged by this step
Unit test: no bone voxel changed its label, the intensity volume is unchanged, and running the modeller twice gives the same result as once
Unit test: the tests of F1-S13 still pass unchanged
stories.notes: Done. softTissue.ts: modelThecalSac(vol, labels, params) runs first in modelSoftTissue; does nothing if any thecalSac voxel exists. Canal per slice = largest bone-enclosed non-bone area within [thecalSac.minCanalAreaMm2 50, canal.maxAreaMm2 1500]; tube of thecalSac.radiusMm 5 round its centroid, kept inside it; slices within the bones' height without a closed canal use the nearest one's outline and an interpolated centre. For real data: in the cervical spine the foramina transversaria are also bone-enclosed holes, but the canal is larger so "largest" picks it.

stories.title: Model the exiting nerve roots at every foramen
stories.description: Extend the soft-tissue modeller: for each foramen centre in the landmarks, on both sides, add a nerve-root tube that starts at the thecal sac, passes through the foramen centre and continues outward and slightly downward for a set length, with a set radius. It never replaces bone. The numbers that shape it live in tools/anatomy/soft-tissue-params.json with "reviewedByOwner": false; only the owner changes that flag. The modeller changes tissue labels only, never the intensity (these structures are invisible on X-ray) and never a bone voxel. Tests run on the phantom with its modelled soft tissue removed (helper in tests/anatomy/: ligamentum flavum, epidural space, nerve root, artery, vein and joint-space voxels turned back into muscle; bone, disc, thecal sac and spinal cord kept), with the phantom's landmarks. Plain TypeScript run in Node (no browser code); only Node's built-in modules, no new dependencies.
acceptance: Unit test on the stripped phantom: every foramen in the landmarks has nerve-root voxels within 2 mm of its centre, on the left and on the right
Unit test: each nerve root touches (is within 1.5 mm of) the thecal sac at its inner end
Unit test: no bone voxel changed its label, and the midline order from F1-S13 still holds
Unit test: a level without a foramen centre gets no nerve root and causes no error
stories.notes: Done. softTissue.ts: modelNerveRoots(vol, labels, landmarks, params) (third step, only when landmarks are given) and a reusable paintTube(vol, labels, path, radiusMm, label, mayReplace). Root = tube (nerveRoot.radiusMm 2) from the nearest thecal-sac voxel through the foramen centre, then outward and 30° downward for 15 mm. Replaces generic tissue, epidural and LF only.

stories.title: Model the facet joint spaces and the SI joint spaces
stories.description: Extend the soft-tissue modeller with joint spaces: non-bone voxels in a narrow gap (a set maximum width) between two DIFFERENT bones. Facet joints: between the bone of one vertebral level and the level directly below, only behind the canal and to its side (so the disc space between the bodies is not counted). SI joints: between sacrum and ilium, on both sides. The numbers that shape it live in tools/anatomy/soft-tissue-params.json with "reviewedByOwner": false; only the owner changes that flag. The modeller changes tissue labels only, never the intensity (these structures are invisible on X-ray) and never a bone voxel. Tests run on the phantom with its modelled soft tissue removed (helper in tests/anatomy/: ligamentum flavum, epidural space, nerve root, artery, vein and joint-space voxels turned back into muscle; bone, disc, thecal sac and spinal cord kept) for the facet joints, and on the pelvis fixture from F1-S11 (a 'sacrum' block and an 'ilium' block on each side with a narrow gap) for the SI joints. Plain TypeScript run in Node (no browser code); only Node's built-in modules, no new dependencies.
acceptance: Unit test on the stripped phantom: joint-space voxels appear on both sides between the L4 and L5 articular pillars
Unit test: every joint-space voxel lies between two different bones — walking outward from it in opposite directions reaches bone of two different levels within the set width
Unit test: no voxel in the disc space between the two bodies becomes joint space
Unit test on the SI fixture: joint-space voxels appear between sacrum and ilium on both sides, and nowhere else
Unit test: no bone voxel changed its label
stories.notes: Done. softTissue.ts: modelJointSpaces(vol, labels, params) (last step so far; needs vol.levels). From every bone voxel, walk 13 directions (axes + diagonals) through air/skin-fat/muscle/joint voxels; reaching bone of a joint-forming level (neighbouring vertebral levels incl. L5-sacrum = facet; sacrum-ilium = SI) within jointSpace.maxWidthMm (4) marks the walked voxels. Facet voxels must be behind the canal front of their slice (sac/cord/epidural min j, filled from the nearest slice); no canal = no facets. On the pelvis fixture diagonal gaps add SI joint voxels up to 2 mm past the ideal gap box at its corners.

stories.title: Model the segmental (radicular) arteries at lumbar levels
stories.description: Extend the soft-tissue modeller: at each lumbar level (L1–L5) with a foramen in the landmarks, on both sides, add a thin artery tube that runs around the side of the vertebral body and into the upper front part of the foramen, next to the nerve root. It never replaces bone or nerve root. This is the vessel that makes transforaminal injections risky, so its exact course is clinical content for the owner to review. The numbers that shape it live in tools/anatomy/soft-tissue-params.json with "reviewedByOwner": false; only the owner changes that flag. The modeller changes tissue labels only, never the intensity (these structures are invisible on X-ray) and never a bone voxel. Tests run on the phantom with its modelled soft tissue removed (helper in tests/anatomy/: ligamentum flavum, epidural space, nerve root, artery, vein and joint-space voxels turned back into muscle; bone, disc, thecal sac and spinal cord kept), with the phantom's landmarks. Plain TypeScript run in Node (no browser code); only Node's built-in modules, no new dependencies.
acceptance: Unit test on the stripped phantom: the L4 foramen has modelled artery voxels within 4 mm of its centre on the left and on the right
Unit test: no bone and no nerve-root voxel changed its label
Unit test: levels outside L1–L5 get no modelled artery
Unit test: the checks of F1-S13, F1-S26, F1-S14 and F1-S15 still hold after all modelling steps are run together
stories.notes: Done. softTissue.ts: modelSegmentalArteries(vol, labels, landmarks, params), run after the nerve roots and before the joints. L1-L5 only; per side with a foramen centre F: tube (segmentalArtery.radiusMm 1) from besideBodyMm (3) outside the body side wall (found by walking from the body centre along x; fallback 15 mm half-width) level with the body centre, to a midpoint, to F + (0, -foramenFrontMm 2, +foramenUpMm 3). Replaces only air/skin-fat/muscle/artery. CLINICAL: the course is a rough draft for the owner to review.

stories.title: Define the manifest and landmarks file formats, with validators and the size check
stories.description: Create src/anatomy/manifestFormat.ts (shared by the converter and the loader; plain TypeScript, validators written by hand, no schema library). The manifest (public/data/manifest.json) lists each region: name (cervical, thoracic or lumbosacral), the levels it covers, its file names (header, intensity, labels, levels, landmarks), size, voxel spacing, source dataset name, licence and attribution text. The landmarks file (<region>.landmarks.json) holds a Landmarks object (src/core/types.ts; the sacrum and iliacCrest entries are optional, but when present they must be complete) and "reviewedByOwner": false. Add validators for both with clear messages, and a function that adds up a region's file sizes and checks the total is 25 MB or less. Commit public/data/manifest.json with an empty region list — the honest state until the real scans are converted with the owner (F1.7). Tests build their tiny input files in memory or in a temporary folder (never real CT data, nothing downloaded).
acceptance: Unit test: a complete example manifest and the phantom's landmarks in file form pass their validators

Unit test: the validators reject a missing field, an unknown region name, an unknown level name, a point with a non-number coordinate, an empty attribution text, and a file name containing a path separator or '..'
Unit test: a landmarks file with sacrum and iliac crest entries passes; a sacrum entry without its endplate and an iliac crest with only one side are rejected
Unit test: the size check passes at 25 MB and fails just above it
Unit test: the committed public/data/manifest.json is valid and lists no regions
stories.notes: Done. src/anatomy/manifestFormat.ts: REGION_NAMES, MAX_REGION_BYTES = 25 000 000, Manifest {formatVersion 1, regions[{name, title, levels, files{header,intensity,labels,levels,landmarks}, size, spacing, sourceDataset, licence, attribution}]}, LandmarksFile = Landmarks + reviewedByOwner, validateManifest / validateLandmarksFile (string[]), parseManifest / parseLandmarksFile (throw), isSafeFileName, landmarksFileName, checkRegionSize(bytes[], limit?). public/data/manifest.json committed with no regions. Added a "title" per region (not named in the spec list) because store.regions needs {name, title} for the picker (F1-S21) - the owner confirmed on 2026-11-12 to keep it.

stories.title: Make the converter run the modeller, write the landmarks file and update the manifest
stories.description: Extend tools/anatomy/convert.ts: after labelling, cropping and resampling, compute the landmarks and run the soft-tissue modeller, then write <region>.landmarks.json next to the region files and add or replace this region's entry in the output folder's manifest.json (other regions' entries stay; source dataset, licence and attribution come from source.json). The converter refuses to finish with an error if the region's files total more than 25 MB, telling the user to choose a larger voxel spacing. Loops only ever run this on generated fixtures in temporary folders — never write real or fixture regions into public/data/. Tests build their tiny input files in memory or in a temporary folder (never real CT data, nothing downloaded).

stories.title: Load a region with loadRegion(name) (loader and unit tests)
stories.description: Create src/anatomy/loadRegion.ts and export it from src/anatomy/index.ts: listRegions() reads data/manifest.json and returns the regions it offers (an empty list if the manifest is missing or lists none); loadRegion(name) fetches the region's header, data and landmarks files, unpacks the gzipped data with the browser's built-in DecompressionStream (only if the bytes really start with the gzip signature — some web hosts unpack .gz files themselves), validates everything with the validators from F1-S8 and F1-S17, and returns { volume, landmarks } where volume matches the shared Volume type. The name 'phantom' returns the synthetic phantom and its landmarks without any download. The region name must be one the manifest lists (never build a URL from unchecked text). Failures (missing file, wrong length, invalid header) reject with a clear message. loadRegion does not touch the store; reacting to the region picker is F1-S21. The fetch function is passed in or defaulted, so unit tests can supply files from memory. The screen tests are the next story (F1-S24). Tests build their tiny input files in memory or in a temporary folder (never real CT data, nothing downloaded).
acceptance: Unit test (Node, files supplied from memory): loadRegion returns a volume with the header's region name, size, spacing, origin and identity orientation and exactly the written intensity, label and level values, plus the landmarks
Unit test: data files served already unpacked (no gzip signature — some web hosts do this) load exactly the same as gzipped ones
Unit test: listRegions returns the manifest's regions, and an empty list for a missing manifest or one without regions
Unit test: loadRegion('phantom') returns the synthetic phantom; a name not in the manifest, a data file of the wrong length and an invalid header are each rejected with a clear message
stories.notes: Done. src/anatomy/loadRegion.ts (exported from src/anatomy/index.ts): listRegions(options) -> RegionEntry[] ({name, title}); loadRegion(name, options) -> {volume, landmarks}; options {fetch?, baseUrl? = "data/"}; PHANTOM_REGION = "phantom" returns createPhantom()/createPhantomLandmarks() without downloads. Names must be listed in the manifest; file names come only from the manifest entry. gunzipIfNeeded checks the 1f 8b signature before using DecompressionStream. Checks header (parseRegionHeader, region name, size vs manifest), data lengths, landmarks (parseLandmarksFile); reviewedByOwner is dropped from the returned landmarks. A missing manifest gives []; an invalid one throws.

stories.title: List the manifest's regions in the store and load a region when one is requested
stories.description: Wire the loader to the shared contract added on 2026-11-10 (src/core/, read-only here): in the anatomy zone's mount(), call listRegions() and put the result in store.regions as { name, title } entries (titles 'Cervical', 'Thoracic', 'Lumbosacral'; an empty list when the manifest has none). Listen for the bus event 'regionRequest' (payload: a region name, sent by the region picker in the carm zone): if the name is in store.regions, load it with loadRegion and put the volume and landmarks in the store; any other name is ignored. A failed load leaves the current volume in place. Loading does not take an image (last image hold): the new region shows on the next image. Register a read-only getter with registerDebugGetter('anatomy', …) so window.__sim.anatomy() returns { loading, lastError } (lastError is a text or null).
